newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Woolworths reports strong sales in units.
newsitem.headline: Woolworths reports strong sales in units.

text.p: Retailers Woolworths Ltd said on Thursday it had seen very strong sales growth in recent weeks, particularly in its Big W and Rockmans stores, after the final quarter of its financial year had started on a fairly flat note.
Managing director Reg Clairs told Reuters the company's full-year result would be much as it had forecast, with sales growth of a little over eight percent.
Clairs said margins had been consistent. "There has been nothing untoward that would impact or affect margins, either up or down," he said.
"There is significant buoyancy in the market, there are signs, very small but some signs, of confidence starting to emerge."
He said the past two weeks had seen a strong resurgence in apparel sales, the strongest surge the company had seen for probably two to three years.
Clairs warned analysts at the higher end of full year net profits forecasts not to have their expectations too high.
"There was some presumption in there that margins would increase. I am not sure that will occur," Clairs said.
Woolworths reported a net profit of A$233.6 million for the year to June 1996.
Clairs also warned that resolution of the so-called "millenium bug" affecting computers at the dawn of 2000 would have an impact on earnings.
"There will need to be an allowance made for this one-off cost...there will be some part of it in this year's result and the majority of it will be in next year's," he said.
Clairs said slower than expected approvals meant the company would have only 13 or 14 petrol outlets operating in Australia by the end of the current financial year rather than the 20 it had planned.
